what_its_for: Pamidronate is used to treat high calcium levels in the blood (a condition called hypercalcemia), bone problems caused by certain cancers (such as multiple myeloma or breast cancer that has spread to the bones), and a bone disease called Paget's disease. It works by slowing down the breakdown of bone, which helps make your bones stronger and reduces pain.
how_to_take: Pamidronate is NOT a pill you take at home. It is given to you as an IV (intravenous) infusion, meaning a nurse or doctor will slowly drip the medicine into a vein through a needle or catheter. Each infusion can take anywhere from 2 to 24 hours depending on why you are receiving it. You will receive this treatment in a hospital, clinic, or infusion center. Do not try to administer this medication yourself.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, kidney function, and body weight. Common doses range from 30 mg to 90 mg per infusion. Treatments may be given once, or repeated every 3 to 4 weeks for ongoing bone problems. Always follow your doctor's specific schedule. Do not ask for extra doses without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: Because pamidronate is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital, it is important to keep all your scheduled appointments. If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion, call your doctor or infusion center as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Do not double up on doses.
storage: You do not need to store this medication at home. Your healthcare team will handle preparation and storage. If you are told you have unused medication at home for any reason, keep it in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep it out of reach of children and away from light. Do not freeze it.
what_to_avoid:
- Do not take other medications that can harm your kidneys (such as certain anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen or naproxen) without your doctor's approval.
- Avoid dental procedures such as tooth extractions, implants, or major dental surgery while on this medication, as pamidronate can cause a rare but serious jaw bone problem. Talk to your dentist before starting treatment.
- Avoid smoking and excessive alcohol, as these can further weaken your bones.
- Do not take calcium supplements or antacids containing calcium within a few hours of your infusion unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
- Tell your doctor about ALL other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting pamidronate.
when_to_call_doctor:
Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience:
- Jaw pain, swelling, or numbness, or sores in your mouth that do not heal (possible jaw bone problem)
- Severe bone, joint, or muscle pain
- Unusual thigh or groin pain (possible thigh bone fracture)
- Signs of low calcium: muscle cramps, numbness or tingling in fingers or toes, seizures, or irregular heartbeat
- Signs of kidney problems: swelling in legs or ankles, decreased urination, or unusual fatigue
- Fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms after your infusion
- Eye pain, redness, or vision changes
- Difficulty breathing or severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of face or throat)
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvements in your calcium levels within 24 to 48 hours after your first infusion. Bone pain may improve within a few days to a few weeks. For ongoing bone protection, the full benefit builds up over several treatments given over months. Your doctor will check your blood tests regularly to see how well the medicine is working.
special_populations:
Kidney problems: Your doctor will check your kidney function before each dose and may lower your dose or delay treatment if your kidneys are not working well. Tell your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease.

Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Pamidronate can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Effective birth control is recommended during treatment.

Children: This medication is not typically used in children. Ask your doctor if you have questions.

Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney problems and low calcium or mineral levels. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
